conflicts.problem: Lesson 2 says Mama Njeri's notebook covers three months (90 days) with P(good day) = 27 ÷ 90 = 0.3. Lessons 1 and 9 describe a 60-day record where about 40% of days were good. The notebook size and the good-day probability (0.3 vs 0.4) conflict, so no Final Explanation can agree with all of them.

Lesson 8's tree gives P(two good days) = 0.36, P(exactly one good day) = 0.48 and P(two bad days) = 0.16. This means P(good day) = 0.6. Lesson 9 (and Lesson 1) put the good-day proportion at about 40%, which gives 0.16, 0.48 and 0.36 respectively. The two lessons contradict each other.
